summary_html: Child achieves **permanency through legal guardianship** or kinship care. Federal programs provide funding parity with adoption for approved relatives.
authority_html:
- **Fostering Connections to Success and Increasing Adoptions Act (FCSIAA)** — kinship-guardianship assistance  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. § 673(d))** — authorizes Guardianship Assistance Program (GAP)

primary_citations.citation_text: New York - N.Y. Soc. Serv. Law § 411 et seq. (Child Protective Services Act – reporting requirements)
New York - Family Court Act Article 10 (Abuse/Neglect juvenile proceedings)

provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: Reversing and ordering a new hearing, the Court held that custody may be taken from a parent and given to a non-parent only on proof of surrender, abandonment, persisting neglect, unfitness, or other like extraordinary circumstances, and that only after extraordinary circumstances are shown may the court decide custody on the child's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: This is the foundational New York authority governing permanency through custody or guardianship with a non-parent.
key_cases.quote: The State may not deprive a parent of the custody of a child absent surrender, abandonment, persisting neglect, unfitness or other like extraordinary circumstances

key_cases.holding: The Court held that awarding custody to foster parents under Social Services Law § 392(6) was impermissible and that the best-interests inquiry for a child in temporary foster care compares continued foster care against discharge to the biological parent or other relative or suitable person, rather than measuring parent against foster parent.
key_cases.relevance: Where a child has bonded with a non-parent caregiver, continued placement may be appropriate even without a finding of parental unfitness.
key_cases.quote: analysis of the child's "best interest" must begin not by measuring biological parent against foster parent but by weighing past and continued foster care against discharge to the biological parent

key_cases.case_name: Smith v. Organization of Foster Families for Equality & Reform
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court reversed, holding that without deciding whether foster parents have a constitutionally protected liberty interest, New York's pre-removal procedures under Social Services Law § 392 and New York City's SSC Procedure No. 5 are adequate to protect any such interest.
key_cases.relevance: It addresses directly whether a long-term caregiver relationship can ripen into a constitutionally protected family interest.
key_cases.quote: the procedures provided by New York State in § 392 and by New York City's SSC Procedure No. 5 are adequate to protect whatever liberty interests appellees may have

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed a termination of an incarcerated father's parental rights and held that, absent legislative authorization, Family Court has no power to order post-termination contact or visitation as a condition of a dispositional order in a contested Social Services Law § 384-b proceeding.
key_cases.relevance: It marks the boundary between adoption, which severs legal ties entirely, and arrangements preserving contact, which require a voluntary agreement or statute.
key_cases.quote: Absent legislative warrant, Family Court is not authorized to include any such condition in a dispositional order made pursuant to Social Services Law § 384-b

timeline_requirements.deadline: Initial hearing commenced within 6 months; each later hearing no later than 6 months from completion of the previous one
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Sixty days after the child was removed from the home (later hearings run from completion of the previous permanency hearing)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in N.Y. Fam. Ct. Act § 1089(a)
Must file TPR or document compelling reason

notice_requirements.timing: No later than 14 days before the date certain for the permanency hearing
notice_requirements.defective_notice_consequence: Not specified in N.Y. Fam. Ct. Act § 1089(b)
